sections.h2: Which Smithtown address do you have?
sections.html:
Smithtown lies on Long Island's North Shore in Suffolk County, with the Sound on its north edge and Islip, Brookhaven and Huntington on the other sides. The name covers more than one place: the town includes the hamlet of Smithtown, plus Kings Park, St. James, Nesconset, Fort Salonga and parts of Commack, Hauppauge and Lake Ronkonkoma. Three incorporated villages sit inside it too, Head of the Harbor, Nissequogue and the Village of the Branch.

That patchwork decides which rules, school district and tax collector apply to your house. A home in Kings Park belongs to a different school district than one in Smithtown hamlet, and a house inside one of the three villages may have village code on top of town code. Check your deed and tax bill for the exact district before you describe the property to a buyer.

Smithtown is a high-value, owner-heavy town where people stay put. Nearly nine in ten homes (88.7%) are lived in by their owners, and the typical value is $669,900. Turnover is low, with 95.0% of residents unmoved in the past year. Population reached 116,847 in mid-2025, a 0.4% gain on 2020.

Mortgaged owners in the town carry monthly costs of $3,809, so a buyer is committing a large budget and will look hard at condition. A house with deferred work is usually priced against that expectation, and a seller who documents repairs and permits starts from a stronger position.

Smithtown commuters rely on a mix of rail and parkways. The Long Island Rail Road's Port Jefferson Branch stops at the Kings Park, Smithtown and St. James stations. By car, the Northern State Parkway reaches the town at Commack, the Sunken Meadow State Parkway winds northeast to Sunken Meadow State Park, and Routes 25, 25A, 111 and 347 carry local traffic. The average commute is 32.2 minutes.

  • Smithtown Central School District, with its own elementary, middle and high school campuses.
  • Kings Park Central School District, which is also based in the town.
  • Portions of the town fall in the Commack, Hauppauge and Sachem districts.

Mention the train station and school district by name in your listing, since those are the first things a Smithtown buyer asks about.

sections.h2: Building Department and certificates of occupancy
sections.html:
The Town of Smithtown Building Department enforces the New York State Building Code and the town's zoning rules, issues permits for new construction, additions and alterations, and grants certificates of occupancy when work is finished. Every transaction is kept on permanent record, which means a buyer's attorney can ask for the permit history of your house.

If you added a deck, finished a basement or converted a garage, find out whether it was permitted and closed out with a certificate. Where it was not, speak to the department before you list. Its office is at 23 Redwood Lane, the phone is (631) 360-7520, and inspections are scheduled at (631) 360-7522 or through an online form.

  • Neighbors and buyers can file a complaint on a property through the department's form.
  • Records requests go through a FOIL form.
  • For a house that has had tenants, ask the department whether any registration applies.

The town's Receiver of Taxes collects town, county and school district taxes on a single bill. The tax year runs from December 1 to November 30, and bills go out once a year around mid-December. The first half is payable by January 10 and the second by May 31, with no grace period for either date.

A partial payment of at least $200 is accepted, and penalties apply only to what is left unpaid. Online and phone payments carry a service fee. The office also takes mailed checks, counter payments and drop-box deposits at the side entrance of Town Hall. The Receiver of Taxes is at 99 W. Main Street in Smithtown. Bring your latest bill to the closing table so the paid half can be credited.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Suffolk County
sections.html:
Deeds for Smithtown property are recorded by the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead, and the clerk's rules are strict. The deed form comes from your attorney or a legal stationer, not the clerk. It must list every party's name and a street address (no P.O. boxes), carry the seller's original signature with a notary's acknowledgment, and describe the property including its village, town and county.

  • A Suffolk County Recording and Endorsement page goes on top, printed on legal-size paper.
  • The RP-5217 transfer report is needed on every deed from November 1, 1980 onward.
  • Form TP-584 is the transfer tax return.
  • Recording fees can be paid by check, cash or money order, but transfer tax needs certified funds, cash, a money order or an approved title or attorney escrow check.

The extra Community Preservation form applies only in the five East End towns, Riverhead, Southampton, East Hampton, Shelter Island and Southold. Smithtown is not one of them, so that form is not part of a Smithtown recording.

The base state transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price. A further 1% charge hits only residential prices of $1 million or more, and it is taken when the deed goes on record.

sections.h2: Selling fast: what a cash sale skips
sections.html:
On a normal listing, you prepare the house, wait through showings and then wait for a buyer's mortgage approval, appraisal and inspection. In a town where condition and permit history draw close attention, each step can reopen the price. A cash sale skips the appraisal and the lender's timeline, and you can close as the house stands. The deed, TP-584 and RP-5217 still go to the Suffolk County Clerk, and the property tax half that is already paid is still credited at closing.

Before you talk to any buyer, gather your latest tax bill, any certificates of occupancy and a list of work done on the house.

faqs.q: Which school district serves a house in Smithtown?
faqs.a: It depends on the street. The town holds the Smithtown Central and Kings Park Central districts, and portions fall in Commack, Hauppauge and Sachem. Your tax bill names the district.

faqs.q: Should my addition have a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: The town issues one when construction is complete, and a buyer's attorney may ask to see it for an addition or conversion. The Building Department can confirm what is on file for your address.

faqs.q: What if the second-half tax payment is late?
faqs.a: Anything postmarked after May 31 cannot be accepted by the Receiver of Taxes. The balance moves to the Suffolk County Comptroller, at (631) 852-3000.

faqs.q: Is Smithtown property tax paid in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The bill splits into a first half due January 10 and a second half due May 31, and a payment of at least $200 can also be made at any time.

faqs.q: Who records the deed on a sale?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead records it, along with the Recording and Endorsement page, RP-5217 and TP-584. Closing professionals usually submit that bundle for you.
